submitter: site_delivery_and_editor lane, fixing bugs_open/466 — the approve-to-apply path, met for the first time on the first paid site (boxingonline, 2026-09-03).
rationale:
The owner pressed APPROVE on a copy edit in the admin queue at 16:21:13Z. The review row went `complete`, the work item it spawned died 17 seconds later at `load_edit_context`, the page never changed, and nothing told him. Two independent defects, either alone fatal.

DEFECT 1 is worse than the bug file first stated, and the measurement is what sharpened it. `include_fields` resolved its names against the REVIEW ITEM'S SPEC (`followSpec[fieldName] = spec[fieldName]`). But `checkpoint_for_review` — the only producer of these items — builds that spec from a FIXED key set: review_data, checkpoint, source_agent, correlation_id, and optionally domain / spec_aspect / on_approve. No arbitrary field can ever be there. [MEASURED 2026-09-03, all history] 21 checkpoint items naming 42 include_fields entries between them since 2026-08-24; ZERO of the 42 present at spec top level, ZERO non-null. This is not two halves disagreeing about where content lives — the lookup is structurally incapable of copying anything, for every consumer, and always has been. The measurement could have come out otherwise: a producer writing the named field at spec top level would show as present_at_spec_top > 0.

DEFECT 2 is a shape mismatch no key-renaming fixes. copy-editor proposes N edits, each with its own page_component_id, slot_name and field_updates; section-editor applies ONE (load_edit_context wants page_component_id OR page_name+slot_name; apply_section_edit takes one field_updates). A two-edit proposal has no single target. Two lanes had already hand-built the fan-out by the time this was found — this lane on 2026-09-03 (items fa49b1bc, 94835c97, both reached complete and both changed the row), and copy_quality_two_stage on review be23d897 on 2026-09-02, whose own resolution text says it was 'replicating the dashboard on_approve contract'. The fix is to make the handler do what two humans independently did by hand.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE SITE: this path is the estate's only human-in-the-loop route for copy changes, and the approval is the exact signal it exists to carry. 16 copy_edit_proposed items are parked in needs_human_review right now, carrying 31 proposed edits between them, none of which can currently be applied by pressing the button.

SCOPE, stated rather than assumed: both new keys default ABSENT, so an on_approve naming neither behaves byte-identically to today — the 2026-08-02 §2 shape (new authority on a shared seam ships opt-in with the unsafe side OFF). I do NOT claim the RFC_022 exemption, because this change wires a live consumer in the same commit (migration 750, copy-editor). The other consumers of on_approve are named below and there is exactly one other, which does not use this handler at all.

plan.summary: Repair `include_fields` (fall back to the approved body when the review spec cannot hold the name — which, measured, is always), and add two opt-in keys to `on_approve`: `fan_out_from` (file one follow-on per element of a named array in the approved data, merging that element's fields at the top of the child spec) and `defaults` (fields the proposal does not carry). Refuse and REPORT a fanned-out element whose page_component_id no longer exists, rather than filing an item guaranteed to die. Record what the approval actually produced on the review row, so `complete` stops being the only thing the approver sees.

edits.rationale: include_fields consults `spec` FIRST (documented semantics preserved exactly — nothing that resolves today can change) and the admin's submitted body second. A name absent from both is now ABSENT from the child spec rather than written as an explicit null; the observed damage was `copy_edit: null, page_target: null`, a shape that reads as real, empty content.

One follow-on per element. Merge order is defaults, then include_fields, then the element's own fields, then the provenance fields LAST — so an element carrying its own `approved_by` or `source_item_id` cannot overwrite who approved it. Children do not duplicate the whole approved payload; `source_item_id` points at the review row, which holds it.

A parked proposal's address rots by DELETION, not only by drift: a rerender REPLACES the page_components row with a new id (LANDMINES, copy_quality_two_stage 2026-08-18). [MEASURED 2026-09-03] 3 of the 31 edits parked in needs_human_review already point at a row that is gone. Filing one produces an item that dies at load_edit_context and tells the approver nothing — the very shape 466 is about, so the fan-out must not manufacture more of it. Scoped to the fan-out path only, so no existing consumer's behaviour changes.

466 candidate 3. A review row reading `complete` while its spawned work failed is 'a complete work item is not a repaired artefact' aimed at a PERSON. The row's result now carries follow_on_items[], skipped_edits[] and fan_out_note; `follow_on_item` is kept for existing readers and names the first. follow_on_item_ids is ALWAYS present in the response, so 'nothing was filed' is a visible [] rather than an absent key that reads as success.

Five tests, and all four load-bearing arms were MUTATION-TESTED rather than merely observed green: removing the dead-address guard, removing the approved-body fallback, making fan-out the default, and dropping the element-field merge each kill exactly the test that names them. The test asserting the opt-in default is the one that matters most to a reviewer — it is what stops a later tidy-up making fan-out unconditional for every checkpoint consumer.

The config half. Replaces the two names that can never resolve with `domain` (a key the review spec genuinely holds, and what the two proven hand-filed items carried), adds fan_out_from='edits' and defaults={edit_type:'content_edit'}. [MEASURED 2026-09-03] of the 41 proposed edits across those 21 items, 41 carry page_component_id, ZERO carry edit_type, ZERO carry page_name — so edit_type must be defaulted and page_name must NOT be, because every edit is addressed by page_component_id and a defaulted page_name would be a guess applied to every page. Snapshot table, anchor guard that aborts if the step has drifted or fan_out_from is already present, and a DO/RAISE verify (a verify block of bare SELECTs cannot stop the COMMIT).

grounded_in: checkpoint_for_review_action.go:157-180 — the review item spec is a FIXED key set: review_data, checkpoint, source_agent, correlation_id, then optionally domain, spec_aspect, on_approve. No arbitrary field can reach it.
site_admin_handlers.go (pre-change) :1240 — `followSpec[fieldName] = spec[fieldName]`, the lookup that could never resolve.

[MEASURED 2026-09-03, all history] 42 include_fields mentions across 21 items since 2026-08-24; present_at_spec_top = 0, non_null = 0. Query: jsonb_array_elements_text(spec->'on_approve'->'include_fields') joined back against `spec ? fld`.
[MEASURED 2026-09-03] 41 proposed edits across those items: 41 with page_component_id, 0 with edit_type, 0 with page_name.

[MEASURED 2026-09-03] of the 31 edits parked in needs_human_review, 3 point at a page_components row that no longer exists, 0 are stale by the updated_at test. (The `complete` bucket's 4-of-4 'stale' reading is artefactual — applying an edit is what bumps updated_at — so that arm of the test discriminates only for unapplied items.)

The other on_approve producer is fork_theme_from_site_action.go:329-337, whose on_approve is {update_theme, update_collection}: no item_type, no include_fields, no `checkpoint: true` — so HandleApproveWorkItem 400s it and it never reaches this code. It is unaffected, and it is the whole of the rest of the population.

Live rows fa49b1bc / 94835c97 (2026-09-03, boxingonline) are the proven target shape this fan-out reproduces: domain, edit_type, page_name, slot_name, field_updates, source_item_id, page_component_id — both reached complete and both changed page_components.
